title: Nine Days in a Chair
subtitle: 应急救援 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 应急救援（灾害防范·救援与急救）
meta: 主题语境：应急救援（灾害防范·救援与急救）　|　核心词汇：ankle　|　正文 316 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 ankle 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1978 my mother twisted her ① ankle on the way to school and walked the rest of the way on it, and said afterwards that the walk was the injury and the step was nothing. My aunt, who was a nurse, said the ankle is the only joint people apologise for, and she had been right about that for thirty-one years; an ankle, she said, is a joint that has never once been thanked.

The ② ankle itself, meaning the joint and not the pain, was nine days of a chair and a bandage and nothing else. She wore ③ ankle socks for the whole of that summer, which my grandmother said was the only honest thing about the accident; an ankle, my grandmother said, is the only part of the body that is measured by socks.

In 1981 the water was ④ up to her ankles in the shop, and she stood in it for six hours because the stock was worth more. The ⑤ ankle injury she had been told to rest in 1978 never healed properly, and she said an injury that never heals is not an injury but a tenant; every ankle, the nurse said, remembers the year it was hurt.

Every ⑥ ankle bandage in the house was the same roll, cut with the same scissors, until 1984. My ⑦ ankle, which I broke in 1986 at the age of nine, was the only thing in the family anybody ever photographed; ankles, my mother said, are the only bones that look like an apology.

The ⑧ ankle she measured in 1990, meaning where the sock should end, was nine inches from the floor and had not changed since 1946. The  ankle I think about is the one she walked on for nine days in 1978, and the  ankle she twisted on the way to school is the only injury anybody in our family has ever been proud of.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: B. n. 脚脖子；踝部（俗称）
E. 固定搭配：twist / sprain one's ankle 扭伤脚踝
F. 固定搭配：ankle socks 及踝袜；短袜
G. 固定搭配：up to one's ankles in ... 深及脚踝的……
H. 固定搭配：ankle injury 踝部损伤

answers.why: twist one's ankle 意为“扭伤脚踝”，1978 年母亲在上学路上扭伤了脚踝，却还是走完了剩下的路。
ankle 意为“踝、踝关节”，踝关节本身——指关节而不是疼痛——就是椅子、绷带和九天，别的什么也没有。
ankle socks 意为“及踝袜、短袜”，那年夏天她一直穿着及踝短袜。
up to one's ankles in ... 意为“深及脚踝的……”，1981 年店里的水深及脚踝，她站在水里六个小时。
ankle injury 意为“踝部损伤”，1978 年医生让她静养的那处踝部损伤从未真正痊愈。
ankle 作定语，意为“踝部的”，1984 年之前屋里每一卷踝部绷带都是同一卷、用同一把剪刀剪的。
ankle 意为“脚脖子、踝部”，1986 年我九岁时摔断的脚脖子，是全家唯一被拍过照片的东西。
ankle 意为“（袜子的）踝部高度”，1990 年她量的那个踝部高度——也就是袜子该到哪里——离地九英寸。
